title: AppProtection profiles: control selection, paranoia level, actions and the default profile

prose.label: Paranoia level.
prose.text: {{paranoia-applies-to}} {{paranoia-range}} {{paranoia-false-positives}} {{custom-paranoia-1}} The profile API schema also carries a paranoia level on custom control items {{gap:custom-paranoia-schema}}. The log fields that record it are in [[zpa.appprotection.logging]].

checks.do: Which profile the rule uses, and whether it is the read-only default, a copy or a custom profile.
The profile's paranoia level and which control kinds it applies to.
Which override mode is set, and the action each control ends up with.
Whether a blocked request matches an always-on Internal Error control that cannot be overridden.

profile-purpose.statement: A profile determines how traffic is inspected and managed: it selects controls and the action taken for them, and is then added to an AppProtection policy.

quotes: AppProtection profiles allow you to determine how traffic is inspected and managed.
After creating an AppProtection profile, you can add it to an AppProtection policy for the Private Access service to use.

control-mix.statement: A profile can select OWASP predefined controls, custom controls, ThreatLabZ controls, WebSocket controls, API controls and Active Directory controls.

quotes: choose from the OWASP Predefined Controls (use the latest version), Custom Controls, ThreatLabZ Controls, WebSocket Controls, API Controls, and Active Directory Controls you have defined.

internal-error-block.statement: Every profile automatically has some OWASP predefined controls from the Internal Error category enabled, with the action Block, and that action cannot be overridden.

quotes: All AppProtection profiles automatically have some OWASP predefined controls from the Internal Error category enabled. They have a default action of Block, and you cannot override the action.

paranoia-applies-to.statement: A profile uses a paranoia level for API controls, ThreatLabZ predefined controls, OWASP predefined controls and WebSocket predefined controls.

quotes: Each AppProtection profile uses a paranoia level if using API controls, ThreatLabZ predefined controls, Open Web Application Security Project (OWASP) predefined controls, or WebSocket predefined controls.

paranoia-range.statement: The Predefined Paranoia Level is chosen from 1 to 4, with 1 described as the highest level of concern and 4 as the least.

quotes: select a paranoia level from 1 to 4, with 1 being the highest level of concern and 4 being the least level of concern.

paranoia-false-positives.statement: Higher paranoia levels check with a wide net of matches and raise the chance of false positives; lower levels use a precise set of matches and give fewer.

quotes: Higher paranoia levels execute checks using a wide net of matches that increases the potential for false positives. Lower paranoia levels execute checks using a precise set of matches resulting in fewer chances of false positives.

custom-paranoia-1.statement: Custom controls, HTTP or WebSocket, have a paranoia level of 1.

quotes: Custom controls (either HTTP or WebSocket) have a paranoia level of 1.

execution-order.statement: When a profile mixes custom and predefined controls, Private Access runs API controls first, then ThreatLabZ, then custom, then the other predefined controls (OWASP, Active Directory and WebSocket).

quotes: Private Access runs API controls first, then ThreatLabZ controls, then custom controls, then other predefined controls (OWASP, Active Directory, and WebSocket).

override-modes.statement: A profile has three override modes, Override None, Override All Controls and Override Specific Controls; Override None is the default, and Specific can set a different action on each selected control.

quotes: This can be as exact as setting a different action for inspecting transaction traffic on each previously selected ThreatLabZ control, OWASP predefined control, WebSocket control, custom control, and API control.
Override None - No override action occurs for any of the controls. This is the default option.
Override Specific Controls - Select the override action for the specific API controls

action-choices.statement: The override actions are Allow, which lets the user proceed to the current URL, Block, which returns a 403 response code, and Redirect, which sends the user to a URL entered in the profile.

quotes: **Allow**: The user is allowed to proceed with the current URL.
**Block**: The user receives a 403 response code.
**Redirect**: The user receives a different URL. Enter an alternative URL that the user is redirected to.
evidence.after: Choose one of the standard override options for all of the API controls, ThreatLabZ Controls, OWASP predefined controls, WebSocket controls, and/or all custom controls:

override-all-for-auto-updates.statement: A profile subscribed to automatic updates for ThreatLabZ controls can only use Override All Controls.

quotes: If you subscribe to automatic updates for ThreatLabZ controls, you can only use the **Override All Controls** option.

threatlabz-subscription.statement: Selecting ThreatLabZ controls offers an Automatically include new control on publish checkbox, and the profile table shows Subscribed to ThreatLabZ as Yes or No.

quotes: you can select the **Automatically include new control on publish** checkbox
**Subscribed to ThreatLabZ**: If the AppProtection profile is subscribed to automatically add new ThreatLabZ predefined controls, **Yes** is displayed.

owasp-version-per-profile.statement: The profile table shows the OWASP_CRS version selected for each profile.

quotes: **OWASP_CRS Version**: The OWASP predefined control version selected for the AppProtection profile.

default-profile-ships.statement: A default AppProtection profile is included with the setup of a Private Access account.

quotes: A default AppProtection profile is included with the setup of your Private Access (ZPA) account.

default-profile-name.statement: The default profile is named Recommended OWASP Top 10 Profile in the AppProtection profile table.

quotes: It is named Recommended OWASP Top 10 Profile in the AppProtection profile table.

default-profile-name.conditions: The legacy reference doc named it "OWASP Top-10 for Visibility". No captured source shows that name; treat it as an older name (likely a UI rename), not as proven wrong. The capture's name is used.

default-profile-readonly.statement: The default profile cannot be edited or deleted.

quotes: The default profile can't be edited or deleted.

default-profile-contents.statement: Using the default template selects the recommended OWASP predefined and ThreatLabZ controls automatically, and some controls are excluded from it for higher efficacy.

quotes: When the default template is used, recommended controls for OWASP predefined controls and ThreatLabZ controls are automatically selected.
Some controls are excluded from the default AppProtection profile for higher efficacy.

copy-profile.statement: The default profile is meant as a template for custom profiles, and any existing profile can be copied to create a new one.

quotes: Use the default profile as a template for custom AppProtection profiles.
Copy an existing AppProtection profile, and use it to create a new AppProtection profile.

default-profile-paranoia.title: Paranoia level of the default Recommended OWASP Top 10 Profile
default-profile-paranoia.detail: Unverified legacy statement: the default profile has "Paranoia Level 1 (conservative)", "permanently set to 1", so tuning higher means cloning it. The profile pages say the default cannot be edited or deleted and do not state its paranoia level. A tenant read of the profile would resolve it.

default-profile-direct-use.title: Whether a policy rule can use the default profile directly
default-profile-direct-use.detail: Unverified legacy statement: the default profile is "Usable directly in policy rules; recommended starting point". The help says to use it as a template for custom profiles and that a created profile can be added to a policy; it does not say the default itself is selectable in a rule.

custom-paranoia-schema.title: Custom controls carry a paranoia level in the profile API schema
custom-paranoia-schema.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "Paranoia Level only applies to predefined controls. Custom HTTP / WebSocket controls don't use Paranoia Level — they're just on/off with a chosen action." The configuring page says custom controls have a paranoia level of 1, and the profile API schema has a paranoiaLevel member on customControls items. How a level of 1 on a custom control affects matching is not stated.
